text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Seven people died in fires over the Christmas holidays. Six died in car accidents.
- Cold weather delayed trains on Boxing Day.
- A panel of doctors and psychologists says that women soldiers can be trained for all of the same war-time duties as men, as long as they are in adequate physical condition. @

- Nokia CEO Jorma Ollila told an Indian newspaper that the company plans to invest 60 million dollars in India over the next five years, first setting up a programming centre and later a mobile phone manufacturing unit.
- Regional newspapers Keskisuomalainen and Ilkka sold their shares in Finnish commercial television operator MTV Oy to media group Aamulehti for 5.4 million markka.
KAUPPALEHTI
- State's net borrowing this year has declined even faster than expected, down to 33 billion markka. @
- Financial Supervision plans to revise its information activities, making them more systematic so there will be less room for sensationalism, says supervision chief Kaarlo Jannari.
- Finance Ministry official Eero Kallio said it looks likely the economy could achieve growth of about four percent next year.

- French bank Paribas says Finnish pharmaceuticals group Orion will be a growth company next year, and that sales of its new breast cancer and Parkinson's disease drugs could rise to 350 million dollars by the year 2003. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- The Baltic Sea is healthier than last year for the first time in a decade, with more seabirds and seals than last year, report says.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish foundries expect 1997 to be their fourth consecutive good year, industry representatives say.
- Brits plan to open paper and pulp futures exchange in Liverpool in November next year, and Swedish derivatives exchange OM also plans to open a similar exchange in London next autumn. @
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET

- A 13-year-old girl died falling from a balcony in an attempt to escape a fire after the firebrigade's skylift failed to work. The lift's hydraulic system was damaged when the vehicle had to move an unlawfully parked car.
